title: Do Justly, Love Mercy
old_p1: Micah was a prophet, a man who speaks for Heavenly Father. Micah asked a big question: “What can I bring to the Lord?”
In those days, people gave animals to the Lord as gifts. Micah wondered, should I bring young calves? Or thousands of sheep?
Then Micah said the Lord has already shown us what is good. The Lord wants good, kind hearts even more than gifts.
old_p2: The Lord wants us “to do justly.” That means be fair and do what is right. He wants us “to love mercy.” Mercy means being kind and forgiving. And He wants us “to walk humbly” with Heavenly Father. Humbly means we listen and know we need His help.
Tonight, think of one kind thing to do tomorrow. Heavenly Father can help you be fair and kind.
p1: Micah asked a big question: “What can I bring to the Lord?” In those days, people gave animals to the Lord as gifts.
Should he bring young calves? Thousands of sheep? Some people brought big gifts but were unkind to others.
So Micah said the Lord has already shown us what is good. He wants kind hearts even more than gifts.
p2: The Lord wants us “to do justly,” being fair and doing what is right. He wants us “to love mercy,” being kind and forgiving. And He wants us “to walk humbly” with Heavenly Father. That is like holding His hand, knowing we need His help.
Tonight, think of one fair, kind thing to do tomorrow. Maybe say “It’s okay” when someone is sorry.
